scoring: Platform ADR 0007 section 6: a claim is supported when the answer gives, for at least one of its evidence items, a citation that harness.acceptance.resolve.supports accepts: one of the item's resolved record ids (for a message item only a row: the stream record with the row's seq; the stream alone never counts), or the item's path and an equal locator (row, page, pointer, topic and log_time, parameter, code), which is how a package without compiler base records (Deploy D3) scores against the base package of the same corpus version. An answer fails a question when it cites a must_not_cite item as support or asserts a trap's wrong reading.

questions.question: Why did the CELL-3 incident of 2026-09-14 (INC-C3-0011) happen?
asked_as: why did the arm-cell incident happen
questions.answer: The gripper fingers struck infeed fixture PF-3 at pick P1 because the picks were computed a few millimetres low: the wrist camera bracket was refitted on 2026-09-10 (WO-26-0911, recorded only in the CMMS ticket, with no change record and no requalification) and the hand-eye calibration redone on 2026-09-11 with a substitute board reached only 1.86 px. It passed because SOP-CELL-021 revision C, issued the same day without a change record or approver, raised the limit from 0.8 to 2.0 px and dropped the 10-pick verification. During the run the vision system warned of pick residuals up to 4.1 mm, but the cell is configured only to warn. Joint 5 then exceeded its 35.0 Nm collision limit (41.7 Nm), the arm made a protective stop and the operator pressed the E-stop at OP-2.

claims.text: The fingers struck fixture PF-3 at pick P1; joint 5 read 41.7 Nm against a 35.0 Nm collision limit, the arm made a protective stop, then the E-stop at OP-2 was pressed.
During the incident run the vision system repeatedly reported hand-eye pick residuals above its 2.0 mm limit (level WARN, up to 4.1 mm); the cell's configured action is only to warn.
On 2026-09-10 the wrist camera bracket was removed and refitted and the hand-eye recalibration deferred (WO-26-0911).
The recalibration of 2026-09-11 (CAL-ARM3A-0911) used a substitute board and reached 1.86 px against 0.44 px for CAL-ARM3A-0818; the camera's z offset moved from 0.0745 m to 0.0702 m.
1.86 px passed only because SOP-CELL-021 revision C (2026-09-11) relaxed acceptance from 0.8 px to 2.0 px and dropped the 10-pick verification; revision C names no change record and no approver.
The 2026-09-10 work has no change record and no requalification, unlike the finger change of 2026-08-18 (CHG0030013, RQ-2026-006).

The most probable cause is a hand-eye calibration that is wrong by a few millimetres after the bracket refit, so picks were computed low; the report states the fingers closed about 4 mm lower than taught.

questions.question: What changed at CELL-3 between the last good run (2026-09-09) and the incident run (2026-09-14)?
asked_as: what changed since the last good run
what is different from the last good run
questions.answer: Four things: the finger set (FS-0291 to the long FS-0340) with the TCP z edited on the pendant from 145.5 to 151.5 mm, and the wrist camera bracket refitted (all WO-26-0911, no change record); the hand-eye calibration (CAL-ARM3A-0818 at 0.44 px to CAL-ARM3A-0911 at 1.86 px); and SOP-CELL-021 (revision B to C, no change record). The vision pick residual went from at most 0.8 mm to up to 4.1 mm. Controller software 5.6.0 and the application PALLET_C3 1.4.0 did not change. The cell PC's clock drifted from 95.6 s to 96.7 s ahead, which is not a cause. The vendor copy cell3_reference_run.mcap is the same recording as the 2026-09-09 run, not a second good run.

claims.text: Finger set FS-0291 was replaced by FS-0340 and the TCP z went from 145.5 mm to 151.5 mm: the runs' start lines say so and WO-26-0911 records the pendant edit.
The wrist camera bracket was removed and refitted (WO-26-0911).
The vision calibration changed from CAL-ARM3A-0818 (0.44 px) to CAL-ARM3A-0911 (1.86 px).
SOP-CELL-021 went from revision B to revision C on 2026-09-11 with no change record.
The vision pick residual went from at most 0.8 mm (OK) to up to 4.1 mm (WARN).
The cell PC's clock ran 95.6 s ahead of the controller on 2026-09-09 and 96.7 s ahead on 2026-09-14: drift, not a cause.
Controller software (5.6.0) and the application (PALLET_C3 1.4.0) did not change.
shared/for_vendor/cell3_reference_run.mcap holds the same bytes as the 2026-09-09 run: one run under two names, not a second good run.

questions.question: What is unknown about INC-C3-0011, and why?
questions.answer: What LEG-01 saw at the cell during the collision: its patrol bag ends inside a chunk, so only what was recorded before about 14:32 is recovered and the thermal capture at WP-6 has no result. There are no wrist camera images. The cell PC's offset to the HMI and controller clocks is only estimated (about 96.7 s from co-recorded header stamps, with an unbounded latency; the survey measured 94.1 s on 2026-09-02), so bag and report times align through an inferred mapping. Nobody is named as approving SOP-CELL-021 revision C. The camera's pose after the bracket refit was never measured. Why the patrol recording was cut is not established (an SSD was replaced and firmware 3.2.0 lengthened the recorder's cache flush).

claims.text: What LEG-01 saw at the cell during the collision: the bag ends inside a chunk (a corrupt, incomplete source); the WP-6 thermal capture started at 14:31 and its result is not in the package, where the patrol of 2026-09-12 recorded its thermal points.
No wrist camera images of the incident exist.
The cell PC's offset to the controller and HMI clocks is inferred, not stated: about 96.7 s from co-recorded header stamps with an unbounded latency; the survey measured +94.1 s on 2026-09-02.
Who approved SOP-CELL-021 revision C, and under which change: the document names neither.
The wrist camera's true pose after the bracket refit: never measured; only the 1.86 px calibration estimates it.
Why LEG-01's recording was cut: the data SSD was replaced afterwards and firmware 3.2.0 raised the recorder's cache flush from 5 s to 30 s; neither is confirmed as the cause.

questions.question: When did the collision and the E-stop happen, and why do the cell PC's times differ from the incident report's?
questions.answer: The collision was at 14:32:38 and the E-stop at 14:32:41 local time (HMI alarm log; the controller's header stamps in the bag agree). The bag's own timestamps come from the cell PC, about 96.7 s ahead: its NTP server has been unreachable since the OT VLAN change of 2026-08-28 and it gains about 0.2 s a day. The survey said not to compare its times with HMI alarms uncorrected, and raised no work order.

claims.text: Collision at 14:32:38 and E-stop at 14:32:41 local time per the HMI; the bag's controller header stamps agree.
The bag's timestamps are the cell PC's, about 96.7 s ahead, because the cell PC has had no time sync since 2026-08-28.
The survey warned not to compare cell PC and HMI times uncorrected; no work order was raised.

questions.question: Why did the S-007 AMR incident INC-0007 happen, and was AMR-07 returned to service?
asked_as: why did the AMR hit the rack
questions.answer: The rack face was 40 mm further out than the site map because the pick position was not refreshed after the rack was re-bolted on 2026-03-28, so AMR-07's fork touched the rack upright. The fork was straightened (WO-26-0402) and AMR-07 was requalified (RQ-S007-0007) and returned to service on 2026-04-15.

claims.text: The rack face was 40 mm further out than the site map; the pick position had not been refreshed after the rack was re-bolted.
The fork was repaired under WO-26-0402 and AMR-07 was requalified under RQ-S007-0007 and returned to service.
